With the proposal cost at 6, continued support now yields a payoff of -4. The coalition therefore withdrew its support.","public_note":"SYNTHETIC — Day 12 public note: The coalition no longer supports the federal carbon-pricing proposal following its latest internal review.","candidate_implication":"When support is withdrawn under SA, subsequent internal records should more often discuss diminished regulatory exposure than deteriorating competitive advantage.","derivation":"Under SA, support responds to the expected burden of alternative regulation; the private notice can change either that burden or competitive benefit. Therefore, withdrawal should be documentarily associated with burden revisions rather than competitive-benefit revisions.","extra_assumption":"Researchers can access internal records that identify which expectation changed."},{"id":"confirmation_SA_03_02","memo":"SYNTHETIC — Day 11 internal memo: The private update lowered the incremental competitive benefit to 2, while the expected burden of alternative regulation remains 12. Under our support criterion, the relevant payoff is 12 minus the proposal cost of 6, or 6. The coalition continues to endorse the proposal.","public_note":"SYNTHETIC — Day 12 public note: The coalition continues to support the federal carbon-pricing proposal.","candidate_implication":"Internal documents may record worsening commercial expectations without any corresponding withdrawal of support when expected alternative-regulation burdens remain high.","derivation":"The notice can reduce competitive benefit while leaving regulatory burden unchanged, and SA bases the decision only on regulatory burden net of proposal cost.","extra_assumption":"Internal deliberations preserve commercially adverse information even when it does not determine the final decision."},{"id":"confirmation_SA_03_03","memo":"SYNTHETIC — Day 11 internal memo: The expected burden of alternative regulation remains 12 after yesterday’s notice. Subtracting the proposal cost of 6 leaves a positive payoff of 6 from continued support. The coalition therefore maintains its endorsement.","public_note":"SYNTHETIC — Day 12 public note: The coalition has ended its support for the federal carbon-pricing proposal.","candidate_implication":"Occasional discrepancies between internal decisions and public statements should be isolated rather than systematically concentrated after unfavorable regulatory-burden updates.","derivation":"The internal decision follows the SA payoff with an independent decision-reversal probability, while public communication independently reports the opposite with probability .05. Independence implies no systematic concentration of communication discrepancies by notice type.","extra_assumption":"Researchers can reliably date and match internal decisions to subsequent public statements."},{"id":"confirmation_SA_03_04","memo":"SYNTHETIC — Day 11 internal memo: Yesterday’s reliable notice reduced the expected alternative-regulation burden from 12 to 2. Continued support would therefore yield 2 minus 6, or -4. The coalition decided not to support the proposal.","public_note":"SYNTHETIC — Day 12 public note: The coalition has withdrawn its support for the federal carbon-pricing proposal.","candidate_implication":"Withdrawals should cluster immediately after internal reassessments that place expected alternative-regulation burdens below the proposal cost.","derivation":"Under SA, the coalition normally withdraws when regulatory burden minus proposal cost is negative. A dated notice followed by a dated decision therefore predicts temporal clustering between downward burden reassessments and withdrawal documents.","extra_assumption":"The timing of private reassessments can be recovered from internal documentary records."},{"id":"confirmation_SA_03_05","memo":"SYNTHETIC — Day 11 internal memo: The notice revised the incremental competitive benefit downward, but the expected burden of alternative regulation remains 12. The relevant payoff from support is consequently 12 less the proposal cost of 6, yielding 6. We continue to support the proposal.","public_note":"SYNTHETIC — Day 12 public note: The coalition remains supportive of the federal carbon-pricing proposal.","candidate_implication":"Where internal records separate regulatory exposure from commercial advantage, recorded support decisions should track revisions to the former more closely than revisions to the latter.","derivation":"SA makes regulatory burden, net of the fixed proposal cost, the decision-relevant quantity; notices affecting competitive benefit do not change that payoff.","extra_assumption":"The available documents distinguish regulatory-exposure estimates from competitive-benefit estimates."},{"id":"confirmation_SA_03_06","memo":"SYNTHETIC — Day 11 internal memo: The notice lowered the expected burden of alternative regulation to 2, making the ordinary support payoff -4 after the proposal cost of 6. Nevertheless, the coalition’s final decision was to continue supporting the proposal, contrary to that payoff signal.","public_note":"SYNTHETIC — Day 12 public note: The coalition continues to support the federal carbon-pricing proposal.","candidate_implication":"Rare internal records should show final decisions explicitly departing from the coalition’s own negative payoff assessment, without requiring a favorable revision in commercial expectations.","derivation":"A burden reduction makes the SA payoff negative, but the independent .05 reversal can still produce support. Thus occasional documents should juxtapose a negative regulatory calculation with continued endorsement.","extra_assumption":"Internal memoranda record both the payoff assessment and the final decision rather than rationalizing the decision afterward."},{"id":"confirmation_SA_03_07","memo":"SYNTHETIC — Day 11 internal memo: The commercial update reduced the incremental competitive benefit to 2. The expected burden from alternative regulation remains 12, so continued support produces a payoff of 6 after subtracting the proposal cost. The coalition maintains its endorsement.","public_note":"SYNTHETIC — Day 12 public note: The coalition continues its support for the federal carbon-pricing proposal.","candidate_implication":"Commercial downgrades followed by continued support should be accompanied by internal references to persistent regulatory exposure when decision rationales are documented.","derivation":"A commercial downgrade does not alter the SA payoff, while an unchanged burden of 12 leaves support positively valued after the cost of 6.","extra_assumption":"Decision memoranda explain which consideration sustained support."},{"id":"confirmation_SA_03_08","memo":"SYNTHETIC — Day 11 internal memo: Yesterday’s notice changed the commercial estimate but left the expected alternative-regulation burden at 12. Because the proposal costs 6, continued support retains a payoff of 6 under our criterion. The coalition remains in support.","public_note":"SYNTHETIC — Day 12 public note: The coalition remains committed to supporting the federal carbon-pricing proposal.","candidate_implication":"Across a sufficiently large documentary series, public support should remain relatively stable after notices concerning competitive conditions but change sharply after notices reducing expected alternative-regulation burdens.","derivation":"Under SA, competitive-benefit notices do not alter the support payoff, whereas a burden reduction from 12 to 2 changes it from 6 to -4; independent low-probability errors add noise without eliminating this contrast.","extra_assumption":"A sufficiently large set of cases permits notice types and ensuing public positions to be classified."}]}
